Makkhali Gosala was indeed the prominent teacher of the Ajivika sect. He was a contemporary of Mahavira (the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism) and Gautama Buddha, and he played a significant role in the development of the Ajivika philosophy.

The Ajivikas believed in fatalism, which is the doctrine that all events are predetermined and inevitable. They held that everything in the universe, including human life, is governed by a cosmic principle called Niyati (destiny or fate), and that human effort cannot alter the course of events.

The state industrial and agricultural exhibition, popularly known as Aligarh Numaish, is held annually in western Uttar Pradesh.

In 1880, on suggestion of Raja Harinarayan Singh the event was named the Aligarh District Fair' during the rule of the collectorate marshall.

It is now called the 'Rajkiya Krishi Udyog Pradarshini - Aligarh'.

India are the most successful team in Champions Trophy history, having won the tournament thrice.

The Men in Blue's first Champions Trophy triumph came as joint-winners with Sri Lanka in 2002 after rain played spoilsport and washed out the final on successive days.

Reigning champions India went on to win the title outright in 2013 and 2025 after beating England and New Zealand in the finals, respectively.

Further insights:

The ICC Champions Trophy is considered the most prestigious ODI cricket tournament in the globe after the 50-over World Cup.

Organised by the International Cricket Council (ICC), the first edition of the Champions Trophy cricket tournament was hosted by Bangladesh in 1998.

At the time, it was called the ICC KnockOut Trophy owing to the nature of the competition.

South Africa became the inaugural Champions Trophy winners after beating the West Indies in the final.

The first couple of editions of the Champions Trophy were held in ICC Associate member nations to increase the popularity of the sport in these regions. Kenya hosted the tournament in 2000.

The tournament was dubbed as the Champions Trophy, and also the Mini World Cup, from the 2002 edition onwards owing to a change in the format of the tournament.

The GST is applicable on the supply of goods or services as against the earlier concept of tax on the manufacture or sale of goods or provision of services. It is a destination-based consumption tax. This means that tax would accrue to the State or the Union Territory where the consumption takes place.

Further insights:

The Goods and Services Tax (GST) is a comprehensive indirect tax levied on the supply of goods and services in India.

It was introduced on July 1, 2017, to replace multiple indirect taxes like excise duty, service tax, VAT (Value Added Tax), and others, creating a unified tax system across the country.

GST is governed by the GST Council, which is chaired by the Union Finance Minister and includes representatives from all states and union territories.

Key Features of GST:

Dual GST Structure:

- CGST (Central GST): Levied by the Central Government on intra-state supplies.

- SGST (State GST): Levied by the State Government on intra-state supplies.

- IGST (Integrated GST): Levied by the Central Government on inter-state supplies and imports.

Tax Slabs:

- GST is divided into four primary tax slabs: 5%, 12%, 18%, and 28%. Certain goods and services, like essential items, are taxed at 0% (exempted), while others like luxury and sin goods attract higher rates.

GST Network (GSTN):

- A technology platform that handles the IT infrastructure for GST implementation, including registration, return filing, and tax payments.

The Minimum needs Programme was introduced in the first year of the Fifth Five Year Plan. The objective of the Programme is to establish a network of basic services and facilities of social consumption in all the areas upto nationally-accepted norms, within a specified time-frame.

The programme is designed to assist in raising living standards and in reducing the regional disparities in development.

The programme is essentially an investment in human resources. The basic needs of the people identified for this programme are Elementary Education, Adult Education, Rural Health, Rural Roads, Rural Electrification, Rural Housing, Environmental Improvement of Urban Slums and Nutrition.

The partition of Bengal was the most important event during the rule of Lord Curzon. It was carried out mainly for the convenience of administration. Bengal in those days was the biggest province of India extending over 1, 89, 000 square miles with a population of 80 million.

The two parts created were:

- Bengal Province: Comprising western Bengal and the Hindi-speaking regions of Bihar and Orissa.

- Eastern Bengal and Assam: Comprising eastern Bengal and Assam, with Dhaka as its capital.

Due to the intense opposition, the partition was annulled in 1911 during the reign of Lord Hardinge, and Bengal was reunified.

Diwani Adalat, in Mughal and British India, was a high court of civil and revenue jurisdiction. It was instituted by Warren Hastings, the British governor-general, in 1772.

There are seven major tectonic plates on the Earth's surface.

The Pacific plate is the largest plate. It is composed entirely of oceanic crust and covers about 1/5th of entire Earth's surface.

The Pacific Plate covers an area of approximately 103 million square kilometers (40 million square miles) and is largely located beneath the Pacific Ocean.

It is responsible for the formation of the Pacific Ring of Fire, a region known for its frequent earthquakes and volcanic activity due to the plate's interactions with surrounding plates.

This port accounts for about fifty per cent of India's iron ore export. New Mangalore port, located in Karnataka caters to the export of iron ore concentrates from Kudremukh mines. Kochchi is the extreme south-western port, located at the entrance of a lagoon with a natural harbour.

· Primary Deficit is the difference between the current year's fiscal deficit and the interest paid on the borrowings of the previous year.

· Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure - (Revenue receipts + Non-debt creating capital receipts).

The largest producer of iron ore in India is the state of Odisha. Odisha accounts for a significant portion of India's total iron ore production, with major deposits located in regions such as Keonjhar, Sundergarh, and Mayurbhanj.

As per the statistics from the Ministry of Mines, Government of India, the production of iron ore at about 253.97 million tonnes in 2021-22 registered an increase of 23.86% over the previous year. Almost the entire production of iron ore (98.62%) accrued from Odisha (53.82%), Chhattisgarh (16.27%), Karnataka (15.88%), Jharkhand (9.74%) and Madhya Pradesh (2.91%) during the year. The remaining 1.38% of production was reported from Maharashtra, Rajasthan, and Andhra Pradesh.

The 24th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1971 made it obligatory for the President to give his assent when a Constitution Amendment Bill is presented to him.

This amendment was enacted to override the Supreme Court's judgment in the Golaknath case (1967), which had ruled that Parliament could not amend Fundamental Rights.

The 24th Amendment was part of a series of amendments (including the 25th and 29th) aimed at restoring Parliament's authority to amend the Constitution, which had been curtailed by judicial decisions.

This amendment was later upheld by the Supreme Court in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), which introduced the Basic Structure Doctrine, limiting Parliament's amending power to the extent that it cannot alter the basic structure of the Constitution.

The physicist who introduced the concept of the uncertainty principle, stating that the position and momentum of a particle cannot be precisely determined simultaneously, is Werner Heisenberg.

· Werner Heisenberg formulated the uncertainty principle in 1927 as a fundamental concept in quantum mechanics. It states that the more precisely you know the position of a particle, the less precisely you can know its momentum, and vice versa.

· This principle fundamentally challenges the classical notion of determinism, asserting that there are inherent limitations to the precision with which certain pairs of physical properties of a particle can be known.

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order with the first part being fixed. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. After a year of B. get to enjoy a C. on the tropical island D. hard work, we finally E. well-deserved vacation
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order with the first part being fixed. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

After a year of

B. get to enjoy a

C. on the tropical island

D. hard work, we finally

E. well-deserved vacation
questions.solution:
After a year of: This introductory phrase sets the time frame for the events that follow. It indicates that something happened following a year of time.

D. hard work, we finally: This part introduces the main action or accomplishment - hard work. The phrase "we finally" indicates that the hard work has come to a conclusion or has yielded a result.

B. get to enjoy a: Following the completion of the hard work, the next logical step is to enjoy a reward. The phrase "get to enjoy a" introduces the idea of experiencing something positive.

E. well-deserved vacation: This completes the thought by specifying what the positive experience is - a well-deserved vacation. The adjective "well-deserved" emphasizes that the vacation is earned after hard work.

C. on the tropical island: Finally, the sentence concludes by providing additional details about the vacation - the location is a tropical island. This information gives context to where the well-deserved vacation is taking place.

Putting it all together, the sentence flows logically from the passage of time to the hard work, then to the enjoyment of a well-deserved vacation, with specific details about the location of the vacation. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

The final sentence: After a year of hard work, we finally get to enjoy a well-deserved vacation on the tropical island.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb and preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Past Indefinite. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Past Indefinite.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + V2 + Object.

For example:

The Champions League was won by Real Madrid. (Passive Voice)

Real Madrid won the Champions League. (Active Voice)

Therefore, the correct answer is option (d): Mary baked the vanilla-flavoured cake for the special occasion celebrated by the family.

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. The social scientists wanted to gets beyond deficit narratives of single life.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

The social scientists wanted to gets beyond deficit narratives of single life.
questions.solution:
In the underlined phrase, the verb 'gets' is in third person singular form (V5) which incorrectly follows the infinitive marker 'to'. A verb that follows the infinitive marker 'to' has to be only in the base form of the verb (V1). Accordingly, the correct option that suggests the correct replacement for the underlined, incorrect phrase is option (d), 'wanted to get'.

Option (a) is incorrect as the plural noun 'scientists' cannot be followed by singular verb 'wants'.

The correct sentence is: The social scientists wanted to get beyond deficit narratives of single life.

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

Note:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

Infinitive marker: A word or affix attached to the stem of a verb in order to form the full infinitive. In English, to is the infinitive marker.

questions.question: Describe how you will say They will deliver the package tomorrow In passive voice.
questions.questionHtml: Describe how you will say They will deliver the package tomorrow In passive voice.

options.text: They will be delivered by the package tomorrow.
options.html: They will be delivered by the package tomorrow.

options.text: The package will deliver them tomorrow.
options.html: The package will deliver them tomorrow.

options.text: The package will be delivered by them tomorrow.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Future Indefinite. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in the Future Indefinite.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + shall/will + V1 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + shall/will + be + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

He will complete the assignment. (Active Voice)

The assignment will be completed by him. (Passive Voice)

The options except (c) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: The package will be delivered by them tomorrow.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.
